To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Cx43 and beta connexins are assembled into connexons in the TGN and that Cx32 mutations associated with X-linked Charcot Marie Tooth disease cause defective folding of Cx32 in the ER.

the site of oligomeric assembly of connexin proteins is the trans-Goligi network, not the ER, that this is a multistep process involving conformational matuuration, and that defective connexon assembly is the molecular basis of Charcot-Marie Tooth disease.

connexins undergo conformational maturing within the ER and then assemble into connexons in the TGN, that this process is essential to the formation of functional gap junctions, and that it is defective in the human disease Charcot-Marie- Tooth disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how gap junctions assemble in the cell.
the molecular mechanisms that govern the folding and oligomerization of connexins, the major gap junction proteins.
the mechanisms by which the cell controls the assembly of membrane proteins, and has uncovered a novel and unexpected mechanism for this control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ER is the site of connexin folding and the TGN is the site of oligomerization.
connexin oligomerization takes place in the TGN for endogenously expressed proteins, and in the ER for overexpressed proteins.
Cx43 undergoes a multilayered conformational maturing process in which folding within the ER is an absolute prerequisite for multisubcellular assembly within the TGN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
connexins are the first known integral membrane proteins that are folded and assembled into their mature multisubunit form after their synthesis.
Cx43 and Cx26 are synthesized in their native conformation, whereas Cx32 is synthesized in a partially folded state that is stabilized by its association with other connexin monomer molecules.

connexins are the first integral membrane proteins to undergo conformational maturing and multisubunit assembly outside the ER, and that the ER is not the site of connexin assembly for endogenously expressed proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Cx43, as well as other beta connexins, are synthesized and folded in the ER, but their assembly into oligomeric connexons occurs in the TGN, a novel paradigm for membrane protein folding, assembly and quality control.
the ER and the TGN can be alternative organelles for multisubunit integral membrane protein assembly.
the site of connexin oligomeric assembly is not fixed and that it is possible to alter it through overexpression.
